Με κέντρο τον Ραχμάνινοφ

Τετάρτη 11 Φεβρουαρίου στις 20:30 | Μέγαρο Μουσικής Αθηνών

The lights dim across the Christos Lambrakis Hall. Two thousand seats fall silent as Alexandra Papastefanou approaches the piano. Her fingers hover above the keys. The hall holds its breath.

Sergei Rachmaninoff wrote music that demands everything from a performer — technical virtuosity, emotional depth, the ability to sustain intensity across vast musical landscapes. His Etudes-Tableaux explore the darker corners of Romantic piano writing, each piece a scene from an inner world of shadow and yearning. Tonight, Papastefanou brings her maturity and interpretive depth to illuminate these hidden dimensions.

The audience at Megaron's classical concerts represents a particular kind of attention. These are listeners who understand that Rachmaninoff requires patience, that the rewards come to those who follow the long arc of his musical thinking. Grey hair predominates but not exclusively — serious students of piano scattered throughout, absorbing what cannot be learned from recordings alone.

Megaron Mousikis provides the acoustic perfection these works demand. The hall's engineering ensures that when Papastefanou's fingers move from whispered passages to thundering climaxes, every dynamic shift reaches the back row with the same clarity as the front. The piano's bass notes resonate through the space without muddiness. The overtones shimmer.

If you need accessibility and familiar melodies, Rachmaninoff's Etudes-Tableaux will challenge you. These are not concert warhorses but demanding works that reveal themselves slowly. But if you're ready for Romantic piano music at its most intense, performed by an artist who's earned her place at this keyboard — Megaron offers exactly what serious listeners seek.
